A specific question helps you choose what to measure. Write your hypothesis before the experiment, and change only one variable as much as possible while keeping other conditions constant. Record the results even when they contradict your expectations; discrepancy is an opportunity to refine the idea. A single experiment is not always enough. Repeat the measurement, search for an alternative explanation, and ask: What evidence might change my mind? This is the beginning of scientific thinking.
